summary: Brendan presents a large-scale algorithmic evaluation of classical price action trading concepts coded and backtested using Claude across 5 years of 1-minute futures data (NQ and ES, totaling 327M simulated trades). Testing over 101,345 rule variations across 10 setups, the study reveals that most price action setups fail on lower timeframes due to transaction costs and lack of edge, while higher timeframes (4h and Daily) show viability. The single most robust configuration surviving locked out-of-sample data is a 4-hour Change of Character (CHoCH) reversal trade with a hard stop, fixed 1:1 risk-to-reward target, New York session filtering, and no pre-condition sweep.

segments.topic: Introduction and Scope of the Price Action Test
key_points: Tested over 100,000 price action concepts using Claude to build an automated testing harness.
Evaluated 40,000 sampled parameter variations plus 61,345 common configurations (101,345 total tested) across 5 years of 1-minute data on NQ and ES futures, generating 327 million simulated trades.
Presenter background: UCLA math/econ graduate, former Raymond James investment banker for 3+ years, full-time algorithmic trading system builder for 2 years.

segments.topic: Core Price Action Concepts and the 10 Setups
key_points: Core mechanics explained: Support/Resistance levels, Trend (higher highs/lows, break of structure), Change of character (CHoCH), Sweeps, Confirmation candles, and Timeframes (1m to Daily).

The 10 major price action setups tested: Level bounce, Breakout, Flip zone, Trend pullback, Trend line, Break of structure (BOS), Change of character (CHoCH), Sweep and reclaim, Supply and demand, and Fair value gap (FVG).
Previewed that Change of Character (CHoCH) held up best, while Sweeps alone reversed only about half the time (~50%).

segments.topic: Testing Methodology, Funnel, and Data Gauntlet
key_points: Addressed subjectivity in manual chart drawing by turning visual rules into quantifiable dials (touches, line vs. zone, confirmation, stop, target, chart, filters), creating 20.3 trillion theoretical combinations.
Tested 101,345 concrete versions: 40,000 spread across dials (4,000 per setup) and 61,345 common settings.

Backtest engine factored in $4 commission per round trip, 1 tick of slippage on entry/market orders, slippage on stops, ambiguous bar losses (if stop and target touched in same minute), and compared against random lines/trades.
Two full years of ES data were kept completely locked away out-of-sample.
Funnel results: Out of 101,345 tested, 88,986 had >=30 trades; 24,879 (24.5%) were profitable after costs; only 8,310 (~8.2%) achieved a Sharpe ratio of 0.5+.

segments.topic: Win Rate vs. Profit and Timeframe Scaling
key_points: Win rate has a very weak correlation with net annual profit (correlation coefficient = 0.27); only 138 strategies won >=80% of trades, and 67 of those used a tiny 1R or sub-1R target.
Timeframe analysis shows trading costs consume 46.0% of gross profits on 1-minute charts versus only 3.9% on daily charts.
Percentage of profitable versions increases from 9.2% on 1m to 47.9% on daily charts.

segments.topic: Level Bounce, Touch Counts, and Flip Zones
key_points: Real horizontal support/resistance levels held 51.1% of touches versus 42.4% for random lines (+8.7 pts edge on NQ, +8.5 pts on ES).

Touching a level more times degraded performance: 1 touch outperformed random by +9.0 pts, while 4 touches only outperformed by +6.1 pts (levels touched 3+ times bounced 19.2% vs 20.5% and broke through 27.8% vs 26.1%).
Flip zones (old resistance becoming support after a break) were the strongest level rule, beating random lines by +11.5 percentage points on NQ and +10.9 percentage points on ES.

segments.topic: Trend Setups, Confirmation, and Stop Types
key_points: Neither Break of Structure (-0.04 ATR) nor CHoCH (-0.05 ATR) produced net follow-through drift on their own.
As a trade setup, CHoCH was the only trend setup with positive median annual P&L (+$61/yr median vs -$328 for BOS, -$368 for sweep/reclaim, -$478 for trendline).
Pairing CHoCH with a sweep lost -$834/yr in unseen data, whereas CHoCH without a sweep made +$903/yr.
Waiting for a confirmation candle gave up 4.3 points of price entry but improved net annual edge by +$719 on NQ.
Hard stops beat close-based stops: close-based stops cost $132 more per year because the larger tail losses outweighed the slightly higher win rate (40% vs 29%).

segments.topic: Final Out-of-Sample Test, Best Strategy, and General Findings
key_points: Context filters: Trading only during New York session (8 AM - 4 PM ET) added +$270/yr; skipping trades into a 3+ day run added +$246/yr; filtering with daily trend hurt performance (-$587/yr).
In the 2-year locked test (which experienced a -22.5% drawdown and a +74.5% rally), only the 4h CHoCH setup survived across both NQ and ES in 4 of 4 trials.
The best configuration (4h CHoCH, hard stop, 1:1 risk/reward target, no sweep) made +$62,179 on 1 NQ contract (61 trades, 54% win rate) and +$39,284 on ES over the 2 locked years.

Reiterated overall pattern: across past testing of 9,000 standard strategies, ICT concepts, and price action, mean-reversion style mechanics (like fading extremes or CHoCH reversals) consistently produce the baseline positive expectancy.

Showed the exact 5-prompt layered specification provided to Claude to construct the data processing engine, behavioral level checks, combinatorial backtester, locked verification window, and visual dashboard.
Emphasized that visual, discretionary concepts must be converted into programmatic rules and stress-tested across out-of-sample market regimes.

claims.claim: Only ~24.5% of tested price action rule sets made money after transaction costs, and only ~8.2% achieved a Sharpe ratio of 0.5 or higher.
claims.caveats: Discovery window on NQ 1-minute data over ~3 years before locked evaluation.

claims.claim: Win rate has little correlation to overall strategy profitability (correlation of 0.27).
claims.caveats: Calculated across 40,000 price action strategy backtests on NQ.

claims.claim: Transaction costs consume 46.0% of gross profits on 1-minute bars but only 3.9% on daily bars.
claims.caveats: Assumes $4 round-trip commission and 1 tick slippage per execution.

claims.claim: Real support and resistance levels hold 51.1% of touches, outperforming randomly placed horizontal lines which hold 42.4%.
claims.caveats: Measured across 5-minute to daily timeframes on NQ.

claims.claim: A level touched 4 or more times holds worse than a level touched only once.
claims.caveats: Levels touched 3+ times bounced 19.2% vs 20.5% for 1 touch, and broke through 27.8% vs 26.1%.

claims.claim: Flip zones hold 11.5 percentage points better than random lines on NQ and 10.9 points better on ES.
claims.caveats: Based on the first retest of broken prior resistance/support.

claims.claim: Requiring a liquidity sweep prior to a Change of Character (CHoCH) entry harms performance (-$834/yr vs +$903/yr without sweep).
claims.caveats: Tested on out-of-sample locked data on NQ.

claims.claim: Close-based stops cost $132 more per year than hard stops despite having a higher win rate (40% vs 29%).
claims.caveats: Holding until candle close results in significantly larger tail drawdowns when levels fail cleanly.

claims.claim: 45% of price action configurations were profitable on 4-hour charts versus only 9% on 1-minute charts during the locked out-of-sample window.
claims.caveats: Tested over a 2-year locked period containing both a 22.5% drop and a 74.5% rally.

visuals.title: The Ten Setups
values_readable: 1 Level bounce: buy support, sell resistance

4 Trend pullback: buy the first dip in an uptrend
5 Trend line: buy a touch of the rising line
6 Break of structure: go with the break of the last swing
7 Change of character: the first break against the trend
8 Sweep and reclaim: a wick through a low, closed back above
9 Supply and demand: the first return to an impulse's base
10 Fair value gap: the first return into a three-candle gap

strategies.name: 4-Hour Change of Character (CHoCH) Reversal
strategies.logic: In an existing trend with higher highs and higher lows (or lower highs and lower lows), wait for the price to close beyond the last swing point in the opposite direction (Change of Character). Enter immediately on the candle close without requiring a prior liquidity sweep.
entry_rules: Identify an uptrend (or downtrend) with 2+ swings.
Wait for a 4-hour candle close below the most recent higher low (for short) or above the most recent lower high (for long).
Do NOT require a prior liquidity sweep.
Enter at the close of the confirming 4-hour bar.
Restrict entries to New York session hours (8:00 AM - 4:00 PM ET).
Skip entries if trading in the direction of a 3+ day consecutive run.
exit_rules: Place a hard stop 1 tick beyond the last swing high/low.
Set profit target at 1R (equal in points to the initial stop distance).
Exit flat at Friday close (16:00 ET) or after 24 to 96 bars.

parameters.name: Trading Hours
parameters.value: 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM ET (New York session)

strategies.stated_performance: +$62,179 on NQ (61 trades, 54% win rate) and +$39,284 on ES across 2 locked out-of-sample years; 66% of 314 common versions were profitable on NQ and 54.5% on ES.
strategies.costs_slippage_detail: $4 commission per round trip, 1 tick slippage on entry and stop orders; ambiguous minute bars counted as complete losses.

strategies.name: Flip Zone Retest
strategies.logic: Identify a confirmed resistance level broken to the upside (or support broken to the downside). When price retests the broken level from the opposite side, enter expecting the former resistance to act as new support.
entry_rules: Identify level formed by 2+ swing points within 0.25 ATR.
Wait for price to close cleanly beyond the level.
On first return/retest within 0.25 ATR of the level, enter long (if broken upward) or short (if broken downward).
exit_rules: Hard stop placed past the prior swing.
Target set at fixed R-multiple or opposite structural level.
strategies.stated_performance: +11.5 percentage points above random lines on NQ; +10.9 percentage points on ES; common daily version produced +$9,093/yr in NQ discovery.
strategies.costs_slippage_detail: Subjected to $4 round trip commission and 1 tick slippage per execution.
